model_interpretation.claim: The baseline assigns one output to each thread in a 32x32 CTA, with neighboring lanes advancing across rows and therefore accessing row-major A and C with strides. This candidate keeps the same 32x32 output footprint but maps lanes across columns and assigns four rows at one column to each thread. That reuses each loaded B value across four independent FP32 accumulators and may improve coalescing while reducing CTA threads from 1024 to 256; the additional per-thread state may affect occupancy. The baseline is the measured one-output-per-thread control; candidate performance remains unmeasured.
model_interpretation.transformations: {"files":["src/candidate.cu"],"retained":["Map each CTA to the same 32x32 output tile as the baseline using a 32x8 block; each thread computes four rows at one column.","Maintain four independent FP32 accumulators per thread and reuse the per-K B value across those outputs; lane columns access B and C contiguously.","Guard row/column tails, use size_t for matrix offsets, and apply alpha/beta once for each valid output."]}

model_interpretation.claim: A 16×16 output tile with a 16-wide K stage should reuse each staged A and B value across multiple output products compared with the naive one-output kernel. This candidate deliberately uses synchronous shared-memory staging as the control; a later asynchronous candidate can retain its tile, lane, and compute mapping so the copy mechanism is the main difference. No speedup is claimed before measurement.
model_interpretation.transformations: {"files":["src/candidate.cu"],"retained":["Replace one-thread-per-output serial dot products with a 16×16 CTA output tile and 16-wide K stages.","Cooperatively stage A and B in shared memory using the same (ty, tx) lane mapping intended for the paired asynchronous candidate; synchronize before consumption and before reuse.","Mask row, column, and K tails with zero-filled loads while preserving full-FP32 accumulation and alpha/beta output semantics."]}

items.subject: Tuilage partagé synchrone avec microtuiles registre
items.objective: Tester l’ajout du staging partagé synchrone 16×16/K=16 de T3 au noyau registre de T2, qui calcule quatre lignes par thread et réutilise B. Partir de T2, préserver ses accès coalescés et calculs FP32, puis vérifier la correction et mesurer si le staging partagé réduit le temps.
